clue.text: Raising prices by 24 — that's not on

definitions.meaning: putting charges up, as a firm does to fares
the answer to 24 across, RAMBLING ON, with its ON taken away leaves rambling, a word for walking in the country

explanation.surface: A complaint that pushing prices up by 24 per cent is unacceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24 is not a number but a cross-reference: 24 across is RAMBLING ON, and without 'on' it is rambling, which is going for a long walk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiking prices is increasing them sharply; hiking is also walking in the hills, a synonym of rambling.

clue.text: Stoned outside English house — expression of resignation follows

indicators.note: the drug word goes outside the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: stoned on drugs means high

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs outside an English home sighs wearily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' is drug slang, not pelted with stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is an interjection voicing weary acceptance or mild disappointment.

clue.text: Eastern leader, one stopping withdrawal of criticism

indicators.note: the numeral plugs the gap, stopping up the other word
a withdrawal is a pulling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: flak is hostile criticism
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An oriental ruler is a person who prevents the retraction of criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: A kalif, more often spelt caliph, is a Muslim ruler regarded as a successor of Muhammad.

clue.text: Sodium discovered in new cavity

parts.note: an atrium is a chamber or cavity, as in the heart

explanation.surface: A chemical element is found inside a newly made hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Natrium is the Latin name for the element, which is why its chemical symbol is Na.

clue.text: Current Democrat drunk in America

parts.note: juice is slang for electricity, the current in a wire
D is the usual abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A sitting Democratic politician turns out to be intoxicated while in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: In US slang someone who has been drinking heavily is said to be juiced, meaning intoxicated.

clue.text: Spread out breads after cover is removed

indicators.note: taking the cover off strips the outermost letters at both ends

parts.note: bun rolls are small breads

explanation.surface: Loaves are laid out once their wrapping is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: To unroll something is to open it out flat, as with a carpet or scroll.

clue.text: Divine tea is brewed in brother's room

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the room word

parts.note: a monk or friar, a brother, lives in a small room called a cell

indicators.note: brewing stews leaves together, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Tea made in a monk's quarters is heavenly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brother' is a monk or friar, whose small room is a cell; 'brewed' looks like it belongs to the tea, but it mixes TEA IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Celestial means heavenly, so it is a synonym of divine as an adjective.

clue.text: Deuce shuffled in decks

indicators.note: cards are shuffled to mix them up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The two of a suit gets mixed into packs of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deuce' is the playing card in the surface, but it is the old euphemism for the devil, as in 'what the deuce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild euphemisms for the devil in exclamations such as 'what the deuce' or 'what the dickens'.

clue.text: Beloved trifles, perhaps I adore you

parts.note: sweet is a term for a beloved, as in 'my sweet'
trifles in the sense of trivial things are nothings

explanation.surface: Sweethearts' desserts, perhaps declaring love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trifles' suggests the pudding, but here it means trivial matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers' murmured endearments such as 'I adore you' are called by this phrase; the phrase is an example.

clue.text: Desire When Eight Bells Toll to be presented progressively

indicators.note: part of the phrase 'to be presented progressively': the first word gives up its opening letter
part of the phrase 'to be presented progressively': the second word gives up its second letter
part of the phrase 'to be presented progressively': the third word gives up its third letter
the position moves on by one in each successive word, so the fourth word gives its fourth letter

explanation.surface: A wish that Alistair MacLean's thriller When Eight Bells Toll be put on, perhaps in instalments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase 'to be presented progressively' is one instruction: letter 1 of When, 2 of Eight, 3 of Bells, 4 of Toll. When Eight Bells Toll is an Alistair MacLean novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Will is a noun for wish or intention, a close synonym of desire.

clue.text: Maybe keep head office development

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle, so a tower is an example of one
block is slang for the head, as in 'knock your block off'

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the head office building project should perhaps be retained.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall multi-storey building put up by developers, often for offices or flats, is this kind of building.

clue.text: Look to one with feminine interior

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the other word, becoming its interior

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed, so to can mean shut
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Advice to examine someone with a womanly inner nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is read as in 'pull the door to', meaning closed. SHUFTI is British slang, from Arabic, for a quick look.
explanation.definitionFit: A shufti is informal British slang for a glance or quick peek at something.

clue.text: Englishman on vacation tipped and got help

indicators.note: a vacated word is emptied of its contents, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: a ship that has listed has tipped over to one side

explanation.surface: An Englishman away on holiday fell over and needed assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist someone is to secure their support, so having enlisted is having obtained assistance.

clue.text: Modern ban on getting stray dog

indicators.note: letters that stray wander out of place, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recent prohibition leads to a dog wandering off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting stray' rearranges MODERN BAN; the 'stray dog' surface pulls 'stray' towards the definition, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dobermann is a breed of dog, named after the German breeder who developed it.

clue.text: Popular brand set in stone

parts.note: brand is an old word for sword, and the most famous one in legend was stuck in a stone until Arthur drew it out

explanation.surface: A well-liked trademark has been permanently fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brand' looks commercial and 'set in stone' looks idiomatic, but both are literal: a sword lodged in a rock.
explanation.definitionFit: In Arthurian legend the young Arthur pulled this famous sword from a stone to prove he was king.

clue.text: Avoid weapons? Not half

indicators.note: only half the word is kept, its first four letters

parts.note: missiles are rocket-propelled weapons

explanation.surface: A question about whether to steer clear of arms, answered with the slang 'not half', meaning very much so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'definitely', but here it keeps half of MISSILES.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something a miss is to skip or steer clear of it, so miss is a synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Stream reversed, as announced at Balmoral?

indicators.note: Balmoral is a royal residence, and the clipped upper-class royal accent pronounces the vowel of back like that of deck

parts.note: a car that has reversed has gone back

explanation.surface: A query about a watercourse turned around, as reported from the royal estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral is the royal family's Scottish castle; in the stereotypical royal accent 'back' comes out sounding like BECK.
explanation.definitionFit: A beck is a northern English word for a brook or small stream.

clue.text: Showing off female's excellent fare

parts.note: brava is the form of the cheer bravo used to applaud a woman
to fare is to do, as in 'how are you doing?'

explanation.surface: A woman's superb food on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a swaggering show of boldness, which is a kind of showing off.

clue.text: This science makes you gloomy yet excited

indicators.note: excited particles are stirred up and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A field of study claimed to make a person miserable yet thrilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Etymology is the scholarly study of the origins and history of words, a branch of linguistics.

clue.text: Setter repeatedly enthusiastic about unopened souvenir

indicators.note: the word is given twice in a row

parts.note: the setter refers to themselves as me

indicators.note: without its opening, so the first letter goes

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: The compiler gushes over a keepsake still in its wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is an object kept as a reminder of a person or event, a keepsake.

clue.text: One mainly expects to see through his work

definitions.text: One mainly expects to see through his work

parts.words: One mainly expects to see through his work
parts.note: a tradesman who fits windows produces something people literally look through

explanation.surface: A person who usually aims to complete a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see through' looks like the idiom for finishing a task, but here it is literal: his work is a pane of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier fits panes of glass in windows, which are transparent.

clue.text: Decay beginning to crack a sign

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: Aries, the ram, is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Rot starting to fissure is an omen.
explanation.definitionFit: Caries is the medical term for tooth or bone decay.

clue.text: Mostly secretive pork-pie manufacturer, one supplying Italian capital

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: cagy, a variant spelling of cagey, means guarded or secretive
pork pie is rhyming slang for a lie, so someone who makes them up tells lies
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A rather furtive maker of pork pies supplies an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for lie. The capital is regional: Cagliari is the capital of Sardinia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagliari is the chief city and regional capital of Sardinia, an Italian island region.

clue.text: Reckless royal officer briefly disrupting plan

indicators.note: the officer breaks into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart of an area
ADC is the short form of aide-de-camp, an officer attending a monarch or general

explanation.surface: A rash courtier briefly throws a scheme into confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes wildly impulsive behaviour, a synonym of reckless.

clue.text: Barmy Sheila, very much so according to Morse

definitions.meaning: barmy is British for crazy or eccentric

definitions.text: Sheila, very much so according to Morse
definitions.meaning: in Morse code the name Sheila is made almost entirely of dots, every letter but the L and A dashes

explanation.surface: A woman called Sheila is said by Inspector Morse to be quite mad.
explanation.walkthrough: In Morse, S, H, E and I are all dots and L and A have only one dash each, so the name is mostly dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotty is British informal for slightly mad or eccentric, and literally means full of dots.

clue.text: Talking incessantly, Nora Batty pinching male jewellery

indicators.note: pinching means nicking, holding the stolen goods inside
batty means crazy, so the letters of the name go haywire

parts.note: bling is slang for flashy jewellery

explanation.surface: Nora Batty, the stockinged gossip of a British sitcom, chats on while stealing a man's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: Nora Batty is a character in the long-running BBC comedy Last of the Summer Wine; her surname is the anagram signal, turning NORA into RAON.
explanation.definitionFit: Rambling on is going on and on without stopping, a phrasal synonym of chattering endlessly.

clue.text: Namely missing old idiot

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: to wit is an old-fashioned phrase meaning namely

explanation.surface: That is to say, a former fool is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Twit is British informal for a silly or foolish person.

clue.text: Monster development having price slashed

indicators.note: slashed means cut, so those letters are cut away

parts.note: progress is advancement or development

explanation.surface: A building project goes ahead at a heavily reduced cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a property advert: a development with prices slashed.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female ogre, a monster of folklore and fairy tale.

clue.text: In boudoir, Henry finally prepared for Agincourt? He did

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the word for the room

parts.note: a bower is a lady's private room or boudoir, in poetic usage

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the name is taken

explanation.surface: King Henry V, in a lady's chamber, readying for the battle of Agincourt.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'He did prepare for Agincourt': the English longbows that won the 1415 battle were made by such craftsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowyer is a maker of longbows, the weapons whose makers equipped Henry V's archers.
